record.original_question: Determine the weight enumerators of generalized Reed–Muller (GRM) codes in general, since the chapter states that these weight enumerators are not known.

evidence.quote: The weight enumerators of GRM codes are not known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $m\ge 1$ be an integer, and fix an integer $
u$ with $0\le 
u\le m(q-1)$. The generalized Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{GRM}_q(
u,m)$ of order $
u$ and length $n=q^m$ over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$ is defined as the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear code
$$\mathrm{GRM}_q(
u,m)=\{(f(\mathbf{x}))_{\mathbf{x}\in \mathbb{F}_q^m}: f\in \mathbb{F}_q[x_1,\dots,x_m],\ \deg f\le 
u,\ \deg_{x_i} f\le q-1\ 	ext{for all }i\}.$$
For a codeword $c\in\mathbb{F}_q^n$, let $\mathrm{wt}(c)$ denote the Hamming weight of $c$, and define the weight enumerator of $\mathrm{GRM}_q(
u,m)$ as the polynomial
$$W_{q,
u,m}(X,Y)=\sum_{c\in \mathrm{GRM}_q(
u,m)} X^{n-\mathrm{wt}(c)} Y^{\mathrm{wt}(c)}.$$

Determine, in closed form, the weight enumerator $W_{q,
u,m}(X,Y)$ for all admissible triples $(q,
u,m)$; equivalently, determine the number of codewords of each Hamming weight in $\mathrm{GRM}_q(
u,m)$ for arbitrary $q$, $m$ and order $
u$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of determining the weight enumerators of Reed–Muller and generalized Reed–Muller codes remains open. Recent work (2024–2025) has computed exact weight spectra for specific small cases (e.g., RM(10,3), RM(10,4), and the fourth-order RM code of length 512) and provided sampling-based estimates for others (e.g., RM(11,5)), but no closed-form solution is known for arbitrary parameters.

status_evidence.title: Reed-Muller Codes: Theory and Algorithms
status_evidence.snippet: Determining the weight distribution of Reed-Muller codes is a longstanding open problem dating back to the 1960s.
status_evidence.claim: The general weight distribution problem for Reed–Muller codes remains unsolved.

status_evidence.title: The weight distribution of the fourth-order Reed–Muller code of length 512
status_evidence.snippet: Determines the weight distribution for a specific RM(4,9) code.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific cases have been resolved recently; the general problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Estimating the Weight Enumerators of Reed-Muller Codes via Sampling
status_evidence.snippet: Provides sampling-based estimates for weight enumerators when exact computation is infeasible.
status_evidence.claim: For many parameter ranges, only estimates rather than exact enumerators are available.
